quote: Unfortunately, we we actually don't anymore. We've kinda moved away from ground mounts just because of how expensive it it tends to be.
stewart_read: This is transparent and honest handling of a genuine hard capability constraint, not a knowledge gap in the negative sense -- the rep knows the policy and states it clearly rather than fabricating a workaround.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as the rep simply giving up on the deal too early, but the ground-mount limitation is a real product gap, not an objection to overcome.
coaching_implication: Affirm the honesty here, but coach the rep to pair the disqualification with a stronger pivot attempt (e.g., partial roof coverage sized to current usage) before offering competitor referrals.

quote: Yeah. I I I really don't wanna put it on the roof.
stewart_read: Customer's roof aversion is a preference-based objection the rep could have flipped by anchoring on the customer's own bill-savings motive stated at 00:43 ('just looking to save money') rather than accepting the refusal after one attempt.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep genuinely believed roof mount was a non-starter after one no. Strategic read is not well supported here since no second angle was tried.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to reconnect refusal moments back to the customer's stated motivator (saving money) as a second angle before conceding.

quote: Oh, okay. But Okay. I was thinking batteries, you know, run run just so I have power at night or something or if some power goes out, I have power.
stewart_read: Customer directly raises battery backup interest -- this maps to Ion's Tesla Powerwall offering, but the rep never names Powerwall and instead tells the customer to look elsewhere ('you can totally look into it. If you can find someone, that's awesome').
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as scope discipline (deferring product specifics to the closer), but the rep doesn't even flag that Ion carries a battery option -- this is a missed opportunity, not appropriate scope-holding.
coaching_implication: This is an uncataloged cross-sell sub-type (battery_storage_inquiry, TBD in schema) the rep should flag: 'We actually do offer Tesla Powerwall for backup -- the design team can include that.' Replay this clip; the rep sent a live lead toward competitors instead of Ion's own product.

quote: I'm gonna refinance and put up another building on the property that's gonna have a wood shop and three parking spots and, you know, power and a bathroom out there.
stewart_read: Customer describes a planned new outbuilding with its own roof and power needs -- an uncataloged variant of the schema's roofing/solar-timing cross-sell logic (solar_for_secondary_structure, not yet a named schema entry) that the rep doesn't probe at all.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep simply logs the call as a future lead. Strategic read that rep is deliberately not chasing a 5-month-out build is plausible given setter scope, but the rep doesn't even ask about the new structure's roof type or size for future design context.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to capture forward-looking cross-sell details (new structure size, roof type, timeline) even when deferring, so the recycled-lead record has real substance for a future call.

quote: Cool. Well, yeah, I'll make a note and take you out for now. But then, yeah, when we can look out to calling you in a few months or looking out for your call and kinda work with you from there.
stewart_read: No date, no specific callback commitment, no confirmed contact method -- this is procedural fragility at the close, not a resolved conditional booking.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as appropriate given the customer explicitly proposed a 5-months-out timeline (a real barrier, not just missing mechanics), pushing this toward conditional_booking. But the rep doesn't even attempt to lock a rough month or confirm who initiates contact, so the mechanics gap stands on top of the real barrier.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to still anchor a rough re-contact window ('I'll reach back out in about 5 months, does that work, or would you rather call us?') even on long-horizon deferrals.

quote: And that house, I got dirt cheap and I got a construction loan on. I'm gonna remodel it completely.
stewart_read: Full home remodel plus later outbuilding construction signals long-term tenure and rising future electric load -- a strong qualifying signal the rep never reflects back or anchors on.
coaching_implication: Point out to the rep that a full remodel plus new construction is a textbook enthusiasm signal (future usage growth); naming it back to the customer ('sounds like you'll be adding a lot of new electric load with that shop') keeps the lead warm for the recycled follow-up.
